core_obligations: Choose a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n] to A and a presentation A' = A[y_1, ..., y_m]/(g_1, ..., g_l), lifting the g_i to elements g'_i of the polynomial ring over R (proof lines 21081-21084).
Take a presentation of M by a matrix (h_ij) over R[x_1, ..., x_n] (proof lines 21085-21088).
Display the presentation of M tensor over A with A' whose matrix has first block (h_ij) and l further blocks g'_i times the identity matrix (proof lines 21089-21095).
Conclude that M tensor over A with A' is finitely presented relative to R, since it is presented by a matrix over a polynomial ring over R (proof lines 21096-21099).

difficulty_reason: The lemma is one of the formal permanence properties of the relative notion of finite presentation introduced in this section: if M is finitely presented relative to R and A to A' is a ring map of finite presentation, then M tensor over A with A' is finitely presented relative to R (statement lines 21072-21077). The proof is a 20-line explicit presentation (proof lines 21080-21099): it chooses a surjection from a polynomial ring onto A, a presentation of A' over A by finitely many generators and relations, a presentation matrix for M over the polynomial ring, and then writes down a presentation matrix for the base changed module whose first block is the old matrix and whose remaining blocks are built from the chosen equations of A' multiplied by the identity matrix. The two things a reader has to check are that the displayed map really is a presentation of M tensor A' and that the matrix has the announced block shape; the author states both and leaves the verification to the reader, so the card records a construction rather than a reduction.
